text: Add impression-time request context (tab, hour, weekday) to the additive user/video-ID scorer.
rationale: This is the only feature family with a positive, directionally consistent train-only temporal-screen lift: +0.00221 primary across all four reported days and full coverage. It is therefore the highest-information first official ablation.
exact_ablation: Extend the seed feature encoder with train-fitted categorical fields tab, hour derived from hourmin, and weekday derived from date; retain the additive model, BCE loss, optimizer, and all other settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.004 because context can alter video ordering within a user.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.003; the screen supports broad ranking lift more strongly than top-five lift.

text: Replace additive user/video effects with a second-order factorization machine over user ID and video ID.
rationale: The seed has only additive ID effects, which cannot express user-video affinity. The measured base-ID screen establishes the safe, available identifier inputs, though it does not directly estimate the interaction-model lift.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed additive linear-ID scorer with a rank-16 factorization machine containing only user_id and video_id embeddings and their dot-product interaction; leave data, loss, training schedule, and early stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.002 to 0.008 if personalized user-video affinities generalize beyond additive propensities.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.006 if affinity interactions promote long-view videos into the top five.

text: Replace the additive ID scorer with an embedding-plus-MLP scorer using only user and video IDs.
rationale: A nonlinear scorer can represent richer ID interactions than the additive seed while retaining the same point-in-time-safe input contract. Direct support for a neural architecture is literature-only, not measured lift evidence.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed additive model with separate 32-dimensional user_id and video_id embeddings concatenated into a two-layer 64-32 ReLU MLP with a scalar logit head; keep BCE, splits, and all non-architecture training choices fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.007 through nonlinear user-video interaction capacity.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.005, with risk of little top-five benefit if sparse IDs are memorized.

text: Use user-normalized BCE so prolific users do not dominate the pointwise training objective.
rationale: The official GAUC is computed within users and positive-count weighted, whereas the seed’s row-mean BCE can be dominated by high-volume users. Available base-ID evidence confirms user grouping inputs exist; no measured group-size analysis is supplied, so confidence is limited.
exact_ablation: Change only the seed BCE reduction: weight each training row by the inverse number of training rows for its user, normalize by total weight, and retain the seed additive architecture and optimizer.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.001 to +0.004; it may improve typical-user ordering but can conflict with the evaluator’s positive-count weighting.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.002 to +0.003 because equal-user pointwise weighting does not directly target top-five positions.

text: Add a within-user RankNet auxiliary loss to the seed BCE objective.
rationale: Within-user positive-negative comparisons are aligned with GAUC, unlike independent pointwise BCE. User IDs and long-view labels are present in the measured base-ID screen, but mixed-label coverage has not been measured, making this exploratory.
exact_ablation: Keep the seed model and BCE unchanged, but add a RankNet logistic pair loss with coefficient 0.25 using uniformly sampled positive-negative pairs from the same user and K=4 negatives per positive.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.006 if same-user mixed-label pairs are sufficiently common and meaningful.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.001 to +0.004 because broad pairwise ordering may not focus errors near rank five.

text: Add an nDCG@5-weighted LambdaRank-style auxiliary loss to seed BCE.
rationale: The official primary includes nDCG@5, so an auxiliary term emphasizing swaps involving ranks one through five directly addresses the metric that ordinary BCE does not target. No measured evidence establishes that valid training slates can be reconstructed; this is high-risk.
exact_ablation: Keep the seed model and BCE unchanged, but add a LambdaRank-style pairwise logistic loss with coefficient 0.1, using detached within-user nDCG@5 swap weights and only positive-negative pairs with nonzero top-five swap weight.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.002 to +0.003 because emphasis on top-five pairs can trade off broad ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.006 if training user groups faithfully represent the compared candidates.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with mixed-user-group ListNet top-one loss.
rationale: A listwise loss can directly train competition among candidates and may benefit top-five ordering. However, the available measured evidence does not establish that all rows for a user form valid contemporaneous candidate groups, so this is a low-priority exploratory alternative.
exact_ablation: Replace seed pointwise BCE with ListNet top-one cross-entropy computed over complete mixed-label user groups, while leaving the additive scorer, data split, optimizer, and training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.004 to +0.003 because group-normalized listwise training can reduce broad discrimination.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.002 to +0.006 if the user grouping is a valid proxy for ranking competition.

text: Add a two-layer deep-cross branch to the ID embedding representation.
rationale: Explicit bounded-order crosses offer a different inductive bias from the seed’s additive score and can capture structured interaction effects. The only measured support is safe base-ID availability; there is no direct screen result for cross capacity.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed additive scorer with 16-dimensional user_id and video_id embeddings followed by a two-layer low-rank deep-cross network and scalar head; retain BCE and all training settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.006 if low-order ID embedding crosses generalize.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.004 if those crosses improve ordering at the head of each user list.

text: Use frequency-aware regularization for user and video ID coefficients in the additive seed.
rationale: The ID-only seed is vulnerable to noisy rare-entity estimates. Frequency is computable solely from training IDs and does not require forbidden outcomes as a feature; no measured frequency-slice evidence is available, so projected upside is modest.
exact_ablation: Change only L2 regularization in the additive seed so each user_id and video_id coefficient receives L2 weight proportional to inverse square root of its training-only ID count, with the existing global L2 as the scale.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.001 to +0.003 through reduced rare-ID overfitting.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.001 to +0.002 because regularization primarily stabilizes general ordering rather than emphasizing top ranks.

text: Switch the seed optimizer from Adam-style updates to Adagrad for sparse ID coefficients.
rationale: The seed consists entirely of sparse categorical ID parameters, for which per-coordinate adaptive updates may change convergence behavior. This is a training-only change; available evidence verifies the base-ID input family but supplies no optimizer comparison.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed optimizer update with Adagrad using learning rate 0.05 and accumulator epsilon 1e-8; retain the additive model, features, BCE loss, batch order, epoch budget, and early stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.002 to +0.003 depending on whether sparse entities converge more reliably.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.002 to +0.002 because optimization improvement need not alter top-five ranking.

text: Add only tab as an impression-time categorical feature to the additive ID scorer.
rationale: Tab is one of the prioritized request-context fields and has full coverage within the only positive feature screen. Isolating it is lower capacity and can reveal whether context gain comes from a robust product-surface signal rather than temporal proxies.
exact_ablation: Extend the seed feature encoder with a train-fitted categorical tab field only; retain user_id, video_id, additive model, loss, and all training settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.003 if tab changes item preference ordering within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.002; a single context field may be insufficient to shift top-five choices.

text: Add only hour-of-day as an impression-time categorical feature to the additive ID scorer.
rationale: Hour is part of the sole positively screened request-context family and is derivable from the logged request-time field. Testing it alone avoids conflating contextual mechanisms in the broader context bundle.
exact_ablation: Extend the seed feature encoder with a train-fitted categorical hour derived from hourmin only; retain user_id, video_id, additive model, loss, and all training settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.003 if time-of-day changes relative item relevance within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.001 to +0.002 because temporal context may improve broad ordering without concentrating gains at rank five.
